clue.text: Farming implement found in park lake

parts.note: P is the map symbol for a car park
a lough is an Irish lake

explanation.surface: An old plough has turned up in the lake of a public park.
explanation.walkthrough: A lough is the Irish word for a lake, as loch is the Scottish one.
explanation.definitionFit: A plough is the tool drawn across a field to turn the soil before sowing.

clue.text: Religious leader interferes over opening of temple

parts.note: someone who pries meddles in others' business

indicators.note: the opening of a word is its first letter, so only that is kept

parts.note: the first letter of temple

explanation.surface: A cleric meddles at the start of a temple service.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'over' places the first piece above the second.
explanation.definitionFit: A priest is an ordained minister who leads worship and performs rites.

clue.text: Passing remarks in cab, editor gets upset about it

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the rearranged letters go round the last word
upset means knocked over and disordered, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: the letters of these two words, to be rearranged
taken as written

explanation.surface: A newspaper editor in a taxi is annoyed by comments made in passing.
explanation.walkthrough: Obiter dicta is Latin for 'things said by the way', used of a judge's incidental remarks.
explanation.definitionFit: Obiter dicta are incidental remarks, especially a judge's comments that are not binding on the decision.

clue.text: Live performance in musical curtailed

indicators.note: curtailed means cut short, so the last letter is dropped

parts.note: Gigi is a stage and film musical by Lerner and Loewe

explanation.surface: A live show of a musical is cut short.
explanation.definitionFit: A gig is an informal word for a concert or live booking by musicians.

clue.text: A drunken bender around eastern city up North

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: around says the jumbled word wraps about the next piece
a drunk staggers about out of line, so the word that follows is jumbled

parts.note: taken as written, to be rearranged
E is the abbreviation for eastern

explanation.surface: Someone goes on a drinking binge in a northern city.
explanation.walkthrough: A bender is a drinking spree, which makes 'drunken bender' read as one idea; 'drunken' is really the signal to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: Aberdeen is a large Scottish city on the North Sea coast, so it is a city up in the north of Britain.

clue.text: Social event in Lincs port causes international incident

parts.note: Boston is a port town in Lincolnshire (Lincs), England
a tea party is a social gathering

explanation.surface: A party held in an English port town sparks a diplomatic row.
explanation.walkthrough: The American Boston took its name from the Lincolnshire town.
explanation.definitionFit: The Boston Tea Party of 1773, when colonists dumped British tea into the harbour, was a famous political protest between nations.

clue.text: Generals fire mostly crookedly in shooting galleries

indicators.note: crookedly means out of straight, so the letters are put out of order
mostly means not quite all, so the final letter of the word before is lost

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written, losing its end

explanation.surface: Army generals shoot inaccurately at the target ranges.
explanation.definitionFit: A rifle range is a place where people practise shooting at targets, like a shooting gallery.

clue.text: Bird employed by Science Museum

indicators.note: employed by suggests something taken on inside a firm, so the letters sit within the following words

parts.note: spans the end of the first word and the start of the second

explanation.surface: A bird has a job at a London museum.
explanation.definitionFit: The emu is a large flightless Australian bird.

clue.text: Short sleep taken by the French in European city

parts.note: a nap is a short sleep
les is the plural form of 'the' in French

explanation.surface: French tourists take a siesta in a European city.
explanation.definitionFit: Naples is a major city in southern Italy, so it is a European city.

clue.text: Bridesmaid on form at broadcast, on in sixty minutes

indicators.note: broadcast means scattered widely, as seed is, so the letters are spread into a new order

parts.note: the letters of these three words, to be rearranged

indicators.note: in places the short word inside the time period that follows

parts.note: an hour is sixty minutes
taken as written

explanation.surface: A TV broadcast slot of an hour features someone in good form.
explanation.definitionFit: A matron of honour is a married woman acting as the chief bridesmaid at a wedding.

clue.text: Mineral one added to drop of Scotch in tumbler, perhaps

parts.note: the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: a drop is only a tiny amount, so just the opening letter of the next word is used

parts.note: the first letter of Scotch
taken as written
a tumbler is one kind of drinking glass, hence 'perhaps'

explanation.surface: A mineral water is poured into a tumbler with a splash of Scotch whisky.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests mineral water and whisky, but 'Mineral' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Isinglass is an old name for mica, a mineral that splits into thin transparent sheets.

clue.text: Dowdy woman, female with strange past

parts.note: F is the abbreviation for female
rum is British slang for odd or strange
P is the abbreviation for past, as in grammar

explanation.surface: A drably dressed woman with a mysterious history.
explanation.walkthrough: Rum here is the British adjective meaning odd, not the drink.
explanation.definitionFit: A frump is an unfashionable, drably dressed woman, so the term describes a dowdy one.

clue.text: Poet reportedly in a thin woollen vest

indicators.note: reportedly means as people say it, so it is the sound of the name that counts

parts.note: Edmund Spenser wrote The Faerie Queene

explanation.surface: A poet is described as wearing a thin woollen vest.
explanation.walkthrough: Spenser the Elizabethan poet and spencer the garment sound the same but differ in one letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A spencer is a short close-fitting garment, in Britain especially a thin woollen undervest worn by women.

clue.text: Sympathise in clubs with old friend entertaining skinflint

indicators.note: entertaining guests means having them inside your home, so one piece holds another

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for clubs in card games
O is the abbreviation for old
a mate is a friend
a skinflint is a miser

explanation.surface: A club member consoles an old pal who is putting up a tightwad.
explanation.definitionFit: To commiserate is to express sympathy or sorrow for someone's misfortune.

clue.text: Supervise throughout diocese

parts.note: over can mean throughout, as in 'over the whole area'
a bishop's see is his diocese

explanation.surface: A bishop is told to keep watch across the whole of his diocese.
explanation.definitionFit: To oversee is to watch over and direct work or people, which is what supervising means.

clue.text: The Queen in Israel, new one in country

indicators.note: in places the royal abbreviation inside the name of the country that follows
new suggests a fresh arrangement, so the combined letters are reordered

parts.note: taken as written
ER stands for Elizabeth Regina
taken as written

explanation.surface: A royal visit to Israel, and then a fresh one to another country.
explanation.definitionFit: Sierra Leone is a country on the coast of West Africa.

clue.text: March show

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to take part in a public protest march
second meaning: to prove or display clearly

explanation.walkthrough: The capital M makes 'March' look like the month, perhaps with a show in it; it is the verb for protesting in the street.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb covers both protesting in a public rally and showing how something works.

clue.text: French flag I unfurled in tense ending to episode

indicators.note: a flag that is unfurled is spread out and loosened, so the letters are opened up and rearranged

parts.note: the letters of these three words, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone unrolls the tricolour at a dramatic moment.
explanation.definitionFit: A cliffhanger is a suspenseful finish to an instalment of a serial, leaving viewers eager for the next.

clue.text: Hack holding page with prominent story

indicators.note: holding means gripping something within, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: to hack at something is to slash it
P is the abbreviation for page

explanation.surface: A journalist keeps a page for a big scoop.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hack' looks like a journalist, which fits the newspaper surface; it is the verb for cutting.
explanation.definitionFit: In newspaper jargon a splash is the main front-page story given big headlines.

clue.text: Change sides in error

definitions.meaning: first meaning: as a verb, to desert to the other camp
second meaning: as a noun, a flaw or fault

explanation.surface: Someone switches allegiance by mistake.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is a verb for deserting to an enemy and a noun for a fault or imperfection.

clue.text: Clinical trial drug giving home unpleasant smell

parts.note: one's place is one's home, as in 'come round to my place'
BO is body odour

explanation.surface: A medicine being tested makes a house smell bad.
explanation.definitionFit: A placebo is an inactive dummy treatment given to a control group in a clinical trial.

clue.text: Seaman found with crack gets pardon

parts.note: AB is an able-bodied seaman
to crack a code or problem is to solve it

explanation.surface: A sailor caught with drugs is let off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Crack' suggests the drug, but it is the verb for working out a puzzle.
explanation.definitionFit: To absolve is to free someone from guilt or blame, a verb meaning to forgive or pardon.

clue.text: Accompanied artist in African capital

parts.note: acc. is the musical abbreviation for accompanied
RA is a Royal Academician

explanation.surface: An artist travels with a companion to an African city.
explanation.definitionFit: Accra is the capital city of Ghana in West Africa.

clue.text: Cut price of lettuce

indicators.note: cut means trimmed short, so the word loses its final letter

parts.note: the cost of something is its price

explanation.surface: Someone notes a reduced price for a lettuce.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cut price' reads as a discount; 'Cut' is really the trimming signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Cos is a variety of long-leaved crisp lettuce, also called romaine.

clue.text: To win only? Precisely

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a bet placed on a horse to come first, with no each-way part

explanation.walkthrough: In British betting a stake 'on the nose' is a bet to win only, not each way (win or place).
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is both betting jargon for a win-only stake and an idiom for exactly right.

clue.text: Have a meal in Neath

indicators.note: in says the letters are found within the place name that follows

parts.note: the middle letters of the place name

explanation.surface: Someone stops for dinner in a Welsh town.
explanation.walkthrough: Neath is a town in South Wales.
explanation.definitionFit: To eat is to consume food, as at a meal.

clue.text: Inn, shortly to be renovated, accommodating earl

indicators.note: accommodating means giving room to, so one piece sits inside the other
something renovated is rebuilt in a new form, so the word is rearranged

parts.note: taken as written, to be rearranged
E is an abbreviation for earl

explanation.surface: A pub is soon to be refurbished and will host a nobleman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shortly' looks like it means 'soon'; it is the word itself that is rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Hostelry is an old-fashioned or jocular word for a pub or inn offering food and lodging.

clue.text: Taking the most optimistic view of a famous footballer? About time

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the earlier pieces go round the next one

parts.note: taken as written
T is the abbreviation for time
George Best was a celebrated Manchester United and Northern Ireland player

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether a star footballer has finally turned up.
explanation.walkthrough: A and BEST together wrap round T. 'About time' reads as an exasperated remark, but 'About' is the wrapping signal.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase 'at best' introduces the most favourable interpretation possible of a situation.
